text:
Take on Irreplaceable You (2018 movie)
So, on a random Sunday, I came across this movie, and my decision to watch it was largely based on its poster. There was a cute girl sitting on the shoulders of a cute, clean-shaven guy with a very prominent dimple. What can I say? The poster did its job.
Going into the movie, I was expecting a deep, moving love story. Sam and Abbie had the history to make it one: childhood sweethearts who had been together for nearly two decades. But somehow, that love never quite translated onto the screen. Or maybe I just didn’t get it.
Abbie seemed determined to stay in control of Sam’s life, deciding who he should date, when he should move on, and even who would take care of him. Sam, on the other hand, seemed rather lost when it came to Abbie. He didn’t quite know how to support her or navigate what was happening between them.
And then there was Dominic, the nurse, who somehow seemed more emotionally invested in Abbie than Sam did.
By the end, Sam’s marriage proposal felt less like a declaration of love and more like an act of pity. Perhaps that wasn’t the intention, but that’s how it came across to me.
For a couple who had spent almost their entire lives together, I expected to feel their love. Unfortunately, I was left wondering whether I had missed something or whether the movie had.
Let me know what you think of it.
label: hot_take

text:
My review of The Nightmare Before Christmas
This was a very good movie. The stop motion was really cool. All of the characters were well written and likable too.
Jack was a really good protagonist. Him being bored with Halloween every year and wanting a change of pace by celebrating Christmas instead made sense. Oogie Boggie was a good villain too. Didn’t have much screentime but he was definitely memorable.
Jack failing Christmas and realizing he should leave it to Santa made sense. The movie was pretty funny too. Sally having visions of Jack celebrating Christmas going wrong just felt like a plot convenience. Wish the movie explained that.
That was the only thing I didn’t like about the movie. Other than that the movie was a solid 8/10. Halloween Town is my favorite world of Kingdom Hearts 1 and 2 so I’m glad I finally watched the movie. Perfect time of the year to.
In my opinion the movie feels like a Halloween movie with Christmas invited. That’s just my opinion though. It does feel like both. It was a really good blend of both holidays.
label: hot_take

Alice in Wonderland (2010), first time watching it after all these years
Finally watched this for the first time. I kept putting it off because the Disney live action remakes don't have the best reputation, and this is the one that started all of that.
I didn't know going in that Alice is 19 in this and it's about her going back. The whole first part with her not remembering any of it worked for me. Depp as the Hatter was a lot, but Helena Bonham Carter as the Red Queen was my favorite part of the movie. Every scene she's in is hers.
The ending lost me a little. It turns into a big battle movie with Alice in armor fighting the Jabberwocky, and it felt like a different movie than the one I was watching. Looked great in parts, but some of the CGI has not aged great either.
Am I wrong on the ending? It seems like people are split on this one.
